description:
You are a forensic engineer analyzing a roller coaster's dynamics. A reference photo of a vertical loop has been placed at '~/Documents/GeoGebra/assets/coaster_loop.jpg'. Your task is to reconstruct the loop's geometry in GeoGebra to prove it is a clothoid (Euler spiral) and not a circle.

1. Import the image into the Graphics view.
2. Calibrate the scale assuming the track gauge (width between rails) is 1.2 meters.
3. Construct a parametric Clothoid loop using GeoGebra's `Curve` command and integrals of trigonometric functions (Fresnel integrals: cos(t²) and sin(t²)). Do NOT just draw a circle.
4. Adjust the curve parameters to visually fit the track center line in the photo.
5. Place a point at the top of the loop and add a text label displaying the loop's height in meters.
6. Save your work as 'coaster_reconstruction.ggb' in '~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/'.
